trigger_condition: tools.readBody(response) rejects mid-drain (e.g. socket reset) before re-auth side effects run
guard_snippet: try { await tools.readBody(response); await markAnalyticsAuthInvalid(...); outcome = await startDetachedSsoLogin(...); } catch (e) { logger.debug(e); }
potential_consequence: Re-auth never triggered; caller's catch returns the now half-drained/errored original 302 to the client

trigger_condition: oauth2-proxy answers the same /oauth2/start redirect with 301, 307 or 308 instead of 302/303
potential_consequence: Confirmed-expired session on those status codes bypasses detection, falls back to the old synthetic-turn behavior this plugin exists to replace

trigger_condition: local clock lags the issuing server so Date.now() < credentials.expiresAt even though oauth2-proxy already redirected
guard_snippet: const confirmedExpired = expiresAt !== undefined && Date.now() >= expiresAt - CLOCK_SKEW_MS;
potential_consequence: Genuinely expired session is treated as not confirmed; raw 302 passes through unlabeled with no re-auth kicked off
